Here is my translation of this Sumerian text:

1. When the day was distant, when day and heaven and earth were [created],
2. When the night was distant, when night and heaven and earth were [created],
3. [When the year] was distant, when destiny was [determined],
4. When the Anunnaki gods were born,
5. When Ama-inana (Inana) had taken up the office of warrior/hero,
6. When Ama-inana distributed heaven and earth,
7. When Ama-inana [...] gave birth,
8. When the gods, their food rations [...] were bound to their dwellings,
9. When the numerous gods were lying down, when the young gods carried burdens,
10. When the gods were digging rivers, heaping up their dirt,
11. When the gods were making clay, establishing its foundation,
12. At that time, with broad wisdom, the blood(?) of the numerous gods being present,
13. Enki, in the engur (subterranean waters), the deep waters, the place where no god's heart was joyful,
14. Was lying in his sleeping place, but sleep would not come,
15. The gods were crying out, they were doing [...] work,
16. The one lying in the holy place, his sleeping place would not allow him rest,
17. Namma, the mother who gave birth to the great gods,
18. Carried the tears of the gods to her son,
19. "You lie down [...] and you sleep [...]"
20. [...] will not arise
21. The form/features of your creature(?) [...] they pleased

**Note:** This appears to be a creation myth describing the primordial times when the gods were burdened with labor, leading to the creation of humankind. This is thematically similar to the Akkadian Atrahasis epic. Some portions are damaged or unclear, indicated by [...] and (?).
